# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book provides a structured introduction to artificial intelligence, connecting foundational ideas to contemporary systems and responsible deployment. It is intended for learners who want to understand both how AI methods work and how their design choices affect people and institutions.

The chapters build progressively. The opening part introduces AI, search, knowledge, planning, and uncertainty. Later parts develop machine learning, neural networks, language, vision, reinforcement learning, expert and generative systems, ethics, production deployment, and future directions. Each chapter includes learning objectives, key terminology, examples, reflection prompts, and further reading.

Readers should have basic programming literacy. Familiarity with introductory algebra, probability, and statistics is helpful, but major concepts are introduced in context.

As an open educational resource, this text may be adopted, adapted, and remixed under the CC BY 4.0 license. Instructors are encouraged to select chapters to match their course, add local examples and activities, and contribute corrections or improvements back to the project.
